title: Constructed cartesian overlap object and transition data
statement: Fix a cartesian square g:X→Y, p′:X→T, p:Y→S, q:T→S, and opens U,V in Y, with shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Paste the cartesian open-restriction square with the given square. Its canonical scheme isomorphism identifies (g inverse U intersection g inverse V).toScheme with the pullback of (U intersection V).ι followed by p along q. Derived pullback along the inverse is the stage equivalence, with inverse derived pullback along the isomorphism; the units and counits come from the fixed composition and identity comparisons [lem-pc-perfect-hom-transport, lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. For the apex, first derive Scheme.Modules.overEquiv on the inverse-image intersection and compose with the stage equivalence [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. These are actual constructions, not witnesses chosen from mere existence. For any L containing U intersection V, overlapOpenInclusionPullbackIso identifies exact nested-open restriction with pullback along the inclusion: compare its underived restriction functor with tensorPullback by uniqueness of left adjoints, and derive by uniqueness of the left-derived functor. perfectOverlapStageObjectIso then applies fixed composition to the cartesian projection equation to compare the actual stage objects. At the apex perfectOverlapApexObjectIso restricts the supplied local isomorphism and uses the inverse nested restriction comparison and the derived site counit. These explicitly construct all object comparisons. overlapLimitTransition is actual derived pullback along the canonical map between the geometric overlap base changes; overlapLimitBaseComparison is perfectHomComparison for that map. The theorem overlapLimitTransition_pin proves by unfolding that conjugation by this comparison is exactly perfectLimitMap.

def perfectOverlapStageEquivalence
    {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) (p' : X ⟶ T) (p : Y ⟶ S) (q : T ⟶ S)
    (h : IsPullback g p' p q) (U V : Y.Opens) :
    schemeDerivedCategory (g ⁻¹ᵁ U ⊓ g ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme ≌
      schemeDerivedCategory (pullback ((U ⊓ V).ι ≫ p) q)
